room.organization: North daylight work band, west-wall reference storage, east reading pocket, and an intentionally open diagonal route from the south entry.
room.main_path: From door_00 at the south wall, move northeast through the open center to chair_01 and desk_01, with a secondary eastward branch to armchair_01.
room.protected_open_space: The south-central turning area and the diagonal strip between door_00, chair_01, and armchair_01 remain free of furniture and use-clearance overlap.

furniture.placement_rationale: desk_01 is the primary work surface, set south of window_00 so daylight reaches the papers from the north while its 0.425 m rear wall gap keeps the full window clearance free. Its local -Y front opens toward chair_01 and the south-central approach, preserving a clear pull-back zone behind the chair.

chair_01 is the wheeled task seat for desk_01, centered on the desk work span with roughly 0.23 m between the chair front and desk front. Its yaw of pi points the local -Y front north toward desk_01, while the clear area south of chair_01 supports rolling back toward door_00.

bookcase_01 occupies the west wall segment above the south door zone, keeping reference books near the work path without narrowing door_00. At yaw pi/2 its shallow depth bears on the west wall and its local -Y front faces east into the room, leaving browsing clearance toward the central aisle.

cabinet_01 is the tall file cabinet on the remaining west wall below bookcase_01, close enough to desk_01 for active folders but separated from door_00 by the south-west wall interval. Its east-facing front and dedicated opening zone avoid forcing a user to cross the chair route for filing.

cabinet_02 is a low equipment and printer cabinet on the east wall, outside the swing and approach of armchair_01. Its local -Y front rotates west, so equipment is reached from the open room rather than from the wall, and it does not block window_00 or the diagonal entry path.

armchair_01 forms the independent reading pocket on the east side, angled west toward the room instead of facing the desk straight on. It is far enough south of cabinet_02 to leave cabinet access, and its west-facing seat keeps the central route visible from the chair while preserving a short approach from door_00.

side_table_01 sits west and slightly forward of armchair_01 at hand height for a book or drink, outside the armchair seat footprint and below the chair_01 pull-back strip. Its neutral yaw is appropriate for a small square support surface and leaves the reading group open toward the room.
